title: Information Technology Act s. 80 — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 80)

content.overview: Power of police officer and other officers to enter, search, etc.. Section 80 provides specified powers to police officers and authorised officers to enter public places, search and arrest without warrant in the circumstances set out by the provision. The analysis must identify the statutory source, territorial or institutional nexus, authority, procedural conditions, digital evidence and available challenge or remedy.

content.study:
Core rule
Section 80 provides specified powers to police officers and authorised officers to enter public places, search and arrest without warrant in the circumstances set out by the provision.

Jurisdictional and procedural test
Start with the place of the relevant computer resource, person, conduct, service or protected system; then identify the statutory source of jurisdiction and the competent authority. Extra-territorial reach does not eliminate the need for statutory nexus or practical enforcement analysis.

Investigation and evidence
Identify the investigating officer/authority, search or process used, preservation requests, devices/accounts, logs and chain of custody. Apply BSA 2023 s. 63 to electronic records where applicable, separately from attribution and weight.

Defences and limits
Test territorial nexus, statutory authority, procedural compliance, notice/due process where applicable, intermediary conditions, consent and constitutional limits. Do not assume that a cyber incident is automatically governed by every IT Act provision.

Current-law caution
Use the provision and rules applicable on the relevant date. Section 66A is not a current offence.

cases.name: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Court reviewed restrictions on online speech under the Information Technology Act.
cases.issue: Whether IT Act s. 66A impermissibly restricted constitutional speech.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 66A was vague and overbroad and violated Article 19(1)(a); it was not saved by Article 19(2).
cases.holding: Section 66A was struck down in its entirety.
cases.relevance: Use only as historical status; do not present s. 66A as a current offence.

cases.name: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer
cases.facts: The Court examined the statutory method for proving electronic records.
cases.issue: Whether electronic records can be admitted without the applicable certificate route.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Electronic records must satisfy the special statutory proof requirements applicable to computer outputs.
cases.holding: The Court reaffirmed the certificate discipline for electronic evidence.
cases.relevance: Use with BSA s. 63 and digital-record admissibility.

cases.name: K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
cases.facts: The Constitution Bench considered privacy as a constitutional right in the digital and modern State.
cases.issue: Whether privacy is protected as a Fundamental Right.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Privacy is intrinsic to dignity, liberty and Part III, subject to legality, legitimate aim, proportionality and procedural safeguards.
cases.relevance: Use for surveillance, data protection and informational privacy.

questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether Information Technology Act s. 80 — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 80) applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
Information Technology Act s. 80 — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 80) is governed by Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles. identify the date, technology, applicable IT Act provision, data regime, intermediary rule and evidence law; distinguish struck-down provisions from current offences.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

questionsAndAnswers.answer:
I. STATEMENT OF FACTS AND PROCEDURAL PROVENANCE
Set out the material facts, forum, procedural stage, notices, pleadings and documents.

II. STATUTORY AND DOCTRINAL SCHEME
Deconstruct Information Technology Act s. 80 — Statutory provision (Information Technology Act s. 80) under Information Technology Act, 2000, allied rules, the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 where applicable, BSA 2023 and constitutional privacy principles, including its purpose, conditions, exceptions and connected provisions.

III. SATISFACTION OF MANDATORY INGREDIENTS
Apply each ingredient to the record, address jurisdiction, limitation, maintainability and the opposing party's strongest objection.

IV. VERIFIED AUTHORITIES
Use the case ratios below only for the propositions they decide and distinguish contrary facts.

V. EVIDENCE AND PRAYER
Address BSA ss. 63, 104 and 109 where relevant, then seek the precise order available from the designated cyber-crime police and criminal court, adjudicating officer, civil court, High Court under Articles 226/227, or competent data-protection and regulatory forum.
